_README: Curated crosswalk from a human candidate indication to the dog or cat condition a companion-animal
program would actually target, and from that condition to the veterinary_indication strings in the
Why this is hand-written: candidate indications are human-phrased and the veterinary corpus is not.
Exact string matching links only 3 of 40. 'Breast cancer' has no dog equivalent - the analogue is
mammary carcinoma. 'Rheumatoid arthritis' is NOT canine osteoarthritis; it is immune-mediated
polyarthritis, and mapping it to the 42 osteoarthritis pairs would have been the headline error of
ASSIGN is ordered and first match wins, following indication_areas.json (A13) - whose own README
records an ordered-regex bug where 'myopath' fired before 'cardiomyopath' and silently filed 11
cardiomyopathies under musculoskeletal. Patterns here are anchored where a general word would
An indication with no bucket, or a bucket whose pattern matches no pair, is rendered as 'no
veterinary evidence retrieved at this indication'. It is NEVER rendered as absence of evidence:
pulmonary arterial hypertension is the largest surviving candidate cluster and carries 2 pairs.
Pair counts are literature attention, not prevalence and not market size. x1's missing_inputs says
so explicitly and that warning governs how these numbers may be read.

Glioma, thyroid carcinoma and shock were added after checking the corpus for dog analogues of the initially unmapped candidates. Renal cell carcinoma has none (0 pairs) and stays unmapped; a bare indication of 'cancer' stays unmapped by design, because it names no dog condition.

lymphoma.label: Lymphoma
lymphoma.why: Canine multicentric lymphoma is the dog analogue and the indication behind the BTK work (A21).

mammary carcinoma.label: Mammary carcinoma
mammary carcinoma.why: Dogs do not get human breast cancer; the analogue is mammary carcinoma. All HER2/ESR1/BRCA/CDK4-6 breast programs map here.

urothelial carcinoma.label: Urothelial carcinoma
urothelial carcinoma.why: Canine urothelial (transitional cell) carcinoma of the bladder.

osteosarcoma.label: Osteosarcoma
osteosarcoma.why: Canine osteosarcoma. Carried here because it is the largest dog oncology literature, though no surviving candidate names it.

mast cell tumor.label: Mast cell tumor
mast cell tumor.why: Canine mast cell tumour, the indication of the only approved canine oncology drugs.

pulmonary hypertension.label: Pulmonary hypertension
pulmonary hypertension.why: Canine pulmonary hypertension, usually secondary to mitral valve disease.

heart failure.label: Congestive heart failure
heart failure.why: Congestive heart failure in dogs, the endpoint of myxomatous mitral valve disease.

cardiomyopathy.label: Cardiomyopathy
cardiomyopathy.why: Feline hypertrophic and canine dilated cardiomyopathy.

hypertension.label: Systemic hypertension
hypertension.why: Systemic hypertension, most often secondary to chronic kidney disease in cats.

mitral valve disease.label: Mitral valve disease
mitral valve disease.why: Myxomatous mitral valve disease, the commonest canine cardiac condition.

atrial fibrillation.label: Atrial fibrillation
atrial fibrillation.why: Atrial fibrillation and feline arterial thromboembolism.

atopic dermatitis.label: Atopic dermatitis
atopic dermatitis.why: Canine atopic dermatitis and records labelled pruritus (5 pairs) - the commercial centre of companion-animal immunology and the IL-4Ra battleground (A20).

immune-mediated disease.label: Immune-mediated disease
immune-mediated disease.why: Immune-mediated haemolytic anaemia, polyarthritis and pemphigus.

inflammatory bowel disease.label: Chronic enteropathy
inflammatory bowel disease.why: Canine chronic enteropathy / inflammatory bowel disease.

osteoarthritis.label: Osteoarthritis
osteoarthritis.why: Canine osteoarthritis, including records labelled degenerative joint disease (3 pairs). NOT the analogue of rheumatoid arthritis, which is immune-mediated polyarthritis.

immune-mediated polyarthritis.label: Immune-mediated polyarthritis
immune-mediated polyarthritis.why: The dog analogue of rheumatoid arthritis. Deliberately separate from osteoarthritis.

glioma.label: Brain tumor
glioma.why: Canine glioma and other intracranial tumours. Brachycephalic breeds are a recognised spontaneous glioma model.

thyroid carcinoma.label: Thyroid carcinoma
thyroid carcinoma.why: Canine thyroid carcinoma. Anchored to exclude hyperthyroidism (11 pairs), which is a different disease - the same trap as osteoarthritis standing in for rheumatoid arthritis.

shock.label: Shock and hypotension
shock.why: Vasopressor use in canine and feline hypotension and shock.
